Fernando, thanks for taking the call. I am Claire Doyle, from the search firm. Before we go into detail, could you walk me through your career?
Of course. I have spent most of my career in advertising groups, and I have been at the helm of finance for fourteen years.
And the most recent one? I see a group here, nine years, which is a long tenure in this market.
I joined that group in 2017 and I left at the end of last year. I spearheaded the consolidation of the back office there, across nine agencies.
Good. Now, our client is Belgian, and the reporting line runs to Brussels. How comfortable are you working in English day to day?
Let me make sure I answer that properly. For five years I reported directly to a CFO in New York, in English, every single day. So the answer is yes, and I can give you an example.
Please do. And then tell me what you bring to the table that a local candidate would not.
Twenty years inside agency economics. I know where the money hides in this industry, and I have already laid that groundwork once, in a group of a similar size.
I have spent most of my career in advertising groups.

Sorry, I did not catch that. Could you say it again?
Let me make sure I answer that properly.
What I bring to the table is twenty years inside agency economics.

Fernando, it's Claire Doyle again. Good news, they want to move to the next stage, so I am putting a call in the diary for Thursday. There will be two people on it. The Group CFO in Brussels, who owns the numbers and will go straight into detail, and the HR director, who runs the process and will ask about your team and your style. Come prepared with two examples of a turnaround you have led, with figures, because he will ask for them. One more thing, and this is important. The whole conversation will be in English, and the Group CFO tends to interrupt with follow-up questions, so do not plan a long speech. Call me back if anything is unclear.

So, briefly. I have worked in media finance for eighteen years now, and I started as a financial analyst in Chicago, which is where I learned to read a client contract properly. I moved into agency work in 2011, and I have been a CFO since 2016. The year I always talk about is 2019, because we lost our largest client, roughly a fifth of the revenue, in a single phone call. I rebuilt the cost base over the following two quarters and we protected the margin, which nobody in the group expected. And the one thing I still have not learned to do well, honestly, is to say no to a good project quickly. I still study it for three weeks first.
